text:
anya: heads up — after the 11:22 deploy I started seeing chart frameskips on large dashboards, canary flagged ~30% slower FMP :eyes:
ben: saw that too, thanks. which dashboard/filters? any repro steps?
maria: linked canary: https://console.internal/canary/3872 — seems worst for multi-heatmap pages with lots of series. telemetry shows parse+eval spike in main bundle.
anya: repro: open Customers > Metrics > 30d, toggle series groups, scroll. CPU main thread spikes for ~600–900ms on first interaction.
tom: deploy-bot reported: "deploy/console v2026.3.11 — splitpoint bundles updated" at 11:22
infra-bot: rollout policy: canary 10% -> 50% (in progress) :rocket:
ben: can you paste the CPU flame snippet?
maria: flame (trimmed):
```
main-thread > parseScript (bundle-analytics-v2.js) 520ms
  parseScript > evaluateModule 210ms
  render > hydrateComponents 180ms
  event handler attach 90ms
```

olivia: that parseScript line stands out — bundle-analytics-v2.js jumped from 180kb->470kb gz after the last merge. who touched the telemetry import?
anya: @maria @ben looks like the telemetry sampling lib pulled a debug artifact, see webpack manifest: `./src/telemetry/index.ts` -> imports `telemetry/debug-sampler` when BUILD_ENV=staging? maybe config mistake.
ben: confirmed. in the canary build the alias resolved to `telemetry/debug-sampler` because of an env mismatch in the CI matrix. quickfix: force alias to `telemetry/production-sampler` and rebuild the canary.
maria: we should also consider deferring telemetry init until after first paint. moving sampling to a microtask or requestIdleCallback could shave the parse/eval hit.
tom: short-term mitigations: rollback canary -> disable rollout, or patch alias + rebuild. long-term: split analytics into a separate async chunk loaded after hydration.
olivia: agree on split. also prefetch rules: our prefetch config currently eagerly fetches analytics chunk for every route, which amplifies parse pressure. we should change prefetch to `prefetch: false` on analytics chunk in the router for heavy dashboards.
anya: can someone patch the alias and flip the canary rollout back to 10%? i'm already seeing user complaints in #support.
ben: pushing PR with alias patch now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4421 — includes test to prevent debug-sampler in production bundle.
infra-bot: rollback suggestion: `reroute canary to 10%` — requires approvals from eng-platform leads.
maria: after PR merges, let's run a canary build and compare gz sizes + telemetry trace. also add a build-size gate on CI for analytics chunk (max 200kb gz).
tom: opened a short-lived ticket for router prefetch change: RD-8293.
olivia: telemetry idea: sample N% at random server-side flag and gate heavy collectors behind flag to avoid per-client init costs. will prototype.
anya: thx all. action list:
- ben: merge alias hotfix + rebuild canary (done as PR link)
- infra: reduce rollout to 10% until rebuild validated
- maria: add CI build-size gate + compare traces
- olivia: prep prefetch change RD-8293
- tom: follow up on async-split plan

ben: merged and kicked a new canary at 11:47.
infra-bot: canary scaled back to 10% at 11:49 per request.
anya: early signal — new canary shows bundle-analytics-v2.js gz 192kb and first-interaction parse down ~260ms. support chatter dropping.
maria: nice. still want async-split tech debt item but this buy us breathing room.
olivia: will draft prefetch patch and link to RD-8293 tomorrow.
anya: closing the loop here, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: thread closed (no activity for 48h)"
